 General technology AI GPT-6.1 Terra makes a strong case for being OpenAI's best bang for your AI buck
 OpenAI's latest model promises big savings without compromising on performance By Stephen Schenck • Oct 26, 2026 — 5:25 PM ET 
 • • Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority Add Android Authority on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover TL;DR 
 OpenAI introduces its latest model, GPT-6.1 Terra, with excellent cost/performance balance.
 While Astra is still OpenAI’s performance king, Terra can offer output quality that’s not much lower, for a mere fraction of the cost.
 Despite similar performance to GPT-6.1 Sol, Terra operates at roughly half the price.
 Progress moves so fast when it comes to all things AI, that “bigger and better” hardly even feels like the target. Instead, we find ourselves tracking developments across multiple fronts, where sometimes it’s just as impressive to find your gains in terms of efficiency — matching the performance of another model for a mere fraction of the cost. That’s exactly the sort of momentum we’re looking at from OpenAI today, as the company shares GPT-6.1 Terra.
 It’s coming up on a month now since we got to meet GPT-6.1 Sol , and today OpenAI introduces its next model to cross the 6.1 threshold, with GPT-6.1 Terra. This follows GPT-5.6 Terra , launched this past summer, and promises big performance and efficiency gains.
 In case you’re having trouble keeping track of them all, GPT-6 Astra is the heavyweight model at the moment, but some concerns have interfered with launch plans for a 6.1 version . GPT-6.1 Sol is basically Astra on a budget, while GPT-6 Luna cares more about keeping costs minimal than approaching Astra’s performance. Terra, as you might surmise, bridges the gap between Sol and Luna, trying to get its porridge “just right.”
 Clearly, then, we’re looking at a model designed to be a slightly cheaper option than Sol, while still coming close to it in terms of performance. But maybe even more impressively, GPT-6.1 Terra manages to outdo itself when it comes to cost-cutting, running with an API cost just 50% that of GPT-5.6 Terra. And sometimes, that low-cost performance even ekes by Astra:
 OpenAI Part of those savings come from being able to get its work done speedier than its peers, and OpenAI says that the new Terra completes computer-use tasks three times faster than the latest Astra and Sol.
 We all know how frustrating it can be to deal with an AI that’s confidently incorrect, and Terra makes some big improvements in this department, too. It demonstrates significantly lower error rates than GPT-6 Luna, while costing roughly half as much as Sol to run.
 Especially for users who have been enjoying what they get from GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra sounds like it’s definitely work checking out. In many tests, it’s right up there offering very similar performance, and almost universally for less money.
 If you’re interested in giving it a try, access gets underway today in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users.
